sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Blank-Check Entity for Public Market Acquisition Mergers (SPAC)

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (bijural: civil law for private law in Quebec under the Civil Code of Quebec, CQLR c CCQ-1991; common law for public law and federal matters; residual federal common law applies to the CBCA and Criminal Code matters)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), in force for Canada 2018
Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), provisionally applied 2017
Canada-China Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA), in force 2014
Convention between Canada and the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation, signed 1986, effective 1987
Canada-United States Tax Convention (1980), as amended by the 2007 Protocol

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), S.C. 2000, c. 17; Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184; Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Suspicious Transaction Reporting Regulations, SOR/2001-317; Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Record Keeping, Verification of Identity and Related Matters Regulations, SOR/2002-186; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46, Part II.1; Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA), R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, ss. 21.1-21.9 (register of individuals with significant control); Budget Implementation Act, 2018, No. 2, S.C. 2018, c. 27. Quebec: Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA), CQLR c S-31.1 (significant-control and beneficial-owner obligations); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1 (mandatory registration, name clearance, and beneficial-owner declaration to the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec); Regulation respecting the registration of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, r. 2.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Articles of Incorporation (ultimate parent entity, where the SPAC is a subsidiary)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec or Corporations Canada, as applicable
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Global Affairs Canada Authenticate Canada Services; 1961 Hague Apostille Convention in force for Canada since 11 January 2024)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Status / Certificate of Compliance (fresh attestation of legal existence and good standing)
Notarial certified true copies of by-laws, board resolutions, and escrow trust authorization
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Quebec notary (Chambre des notaires du Quebec)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Extract of the Register of Individuals with Significant Control (UBO register)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille plus certified French or English translation

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA), CQLR c S-31.1, ss. 20-34 (articles of incorporation), ss. 86-107 (registered office and records), ss. 108-198 (directors and officers); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), Legal Publicity Division
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts de constitution (Articles of Incorporation) filed electronically through the CLIP portal of the Registraire des entreprises
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Quebec business corporation; nominal consideration per share is permitted. For SPAC operations, all IPO and underwriting proceeds must be deposited into a Canadian trust escrow account governed by a declaration of trust and released only for a qualified initial business combination, shareholder redemption, or distribution, in accordance with AMF securities rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED that the incorporator's subscription for one hundred Common Shares at nominal stated capital is accepted, and the subscription funds are deposited in the Corporation's escrow trust account in accordance with applicable Quebec securities law. FURTHER RESOLVED that the registered office of the Corporation is established at the principal establishment address in Quebec and the Registraire des entreprises is directed to record it. FURTHER RESOLVED that the directors named in the Articles hold office, and that the President and Secretary-Treasurer are appointed. FURTHER RESOLVED that the officers are authorized to open and maintain a trust escrow account and an operating account, execute banking resolutions, and complete all statutory filings with the Registraire and the Autorité des marchés financiers.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - CLIP online service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request through the REQ's CLIP portal, specifying the proposed corporate name with the legal ending 'Inc.', and remit the NUANS search results. For a SPAC vehicle, the name must not imply banking, trust, or insurance activity unless separately licensed. The REQ issues a name reservation certificate valid for 90 days, which must accompany the articles upon filing.
required_dossiers: Proof of identity for signing incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused, the incorporator may submit a revised name application with a written distinctiveness or trademark argument; a review may also be requested with the REQ within 30 days of refusal, and no additional state fee applies for the substituted name in the same reservation cycle.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Statuts de constitution in French or English, setting out the corporate name, share structure (authorized classes with SPAC vote entitlements), restrictions on share transfer, business restrictions, and the number of directors. The articles are executed by the incorporator and, for electronic filing, certified by an approved lawyer or notary attesting to the identity and capacity of the signatory.
required_dossiers: Signed Articles of Incorporation (Statuts de constitution)
Form to establish a legal person (immatriculation form)
Certification of the incorporator by lawyer or notary
Consent to act as directors (to be filed with REQ)

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Submission, Fee Payment, and Issuance of Certificate of Constitution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - CLIP electronic filing window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the certified articles and enterprise registration form through the CLIP portal, pay the prescribed filing and enterprise registration duties, and receive the Certificate of Constitution and the enterprise registration number in the Quebec enterprise register. There is no minimum paid-up capital condition precedent to issuance of the certificate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the REQ issues a query concerning signature attestation, fees, or share provisions, the filing counsel shall file a corrective attestation and supporting resolution within 5 business days; corrected articles may be refiled without duplicate state fee where the REQ determines the correction was within the original filing intent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Organizational Meeting and Board Governance Adoption
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporation - Board of Directors and Registered Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first organizational meeting of the incorporator and the appointed directors: adopt the by-laws of the Corporation, fix the registered office address in Quebec, ratify the subscription for Common Shares, elect the President and Secretary-Treasurer, and authorize the opening of a trust escrow account and an operating account with a Canadian Schedule I bank. Record the organizational resolutions in the corporate minute book and issue share certificates.
required_dossiers: Bank account opening dossiers with AML/KYC attestation and trust escrow declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the minutes are challenged for non-compliance, the directors may call a subsequent meeting and ratify all actions by waiver of notice; such waiver and ratification cure procedural defaults under the QBCA without additional state filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax Registrations and AMF Blank-Check Issuer Notices
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec; Canada Revenue Agency (CRA); Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the Corporation for Quebec and federal tax accounts: obtain a CRA business number for the T2 corporate income tax account, and register with Revenu Québec for GST/QST and employer source deductions. File with the AMF any required notice of intention to become a reporting issuer or a blank-check issuer exemption undertaking, and execute the trust escrow agreement stipulating SWIFT wire rails and release conditions for the SPAC proceeds.
required_dossiers: CRA Business Number request (RC1 or online)
Revenu Québec registration form (LM-101 or CLIP)
SPAC trust escrow agreement / declaration of trust
AMF blank-check issuer notice or exemption filing
Directors' authorization for SWIFT wire and escrow release instructions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AMF queries the blank-check issuer status or the escrow arrangement, filing counsel shall submit a supplemental undertaking and, where required, apply for discretionary relief under section 310 of the Quebec Securities Act (LSVM); concurrent revisions to the declaration of trust may be made with bank approval.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) - Securities Division
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registration as a Reporting Issuer (Blank-Check Issuer) under the Quebec Securities Act (Loi sur les valeurs mobilières, LSVM), including the prospectus escrow undertaking required for special purpose acquisition companies

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Administrative Office Occupancy Only; no industrial facility, no process emissions, and no contaminant discharge sources applicable to the SPAC's principal establishment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for office-only occupancy; if the SPAC later controls an operating portfolio company in Quebec, the portfolio entity must meet MELCCFP process wastewater limits of 15 mg/L BOD5, 30 mg/L TSS, and pH 6.0-9.5, and air contaminant thresholds under the Règlement sur l'assainissement de l'atmosphère for VOCs; all hazardous waste must follow the Regulation respecting hazardous materials (REIMR) traceability.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety attestation (RP-1 certification) for the registered office issued by the municipal fire prevention service; structural load inspection is waived for Class B office occupancy but a certification of compliant occupancy load is required from the building owner; workplace clearance from CNESST (Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail) covering evacuation plan, first aid equipment, and office ergonomics compliance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — federal corporate income tax (T2) and GST/HST, administered through the CRA 'My Business Account' portal (canada.ca); and Revenu Québec — Quebec Sales Tax (QST), Quebec income tax, and payroll contributions, administered through the Revenu Québec 'Espace client' portal (revenuquebec.ca). Federal and provincial registrations are integrated with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec's Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ) and the CRA Business Number (BN).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign sponsor must: (1) incorporate the SPAC under the CBCA or the Quebec Business Corporations Act and obtain the NEQ from the Registraire des entreprises; (2) apply through CRA Business Registration Online for a BN with a GST/HST (RT) program account and a corporation income tax account; (3) register for QST with Revenu Québec using Form LM-1-V and the same BN/NEQ; (4) open a payroll (RP) account if directors' fees are paid. Registration is fully electronic, is typically completed within 5-10 business days, requires no Canadian physical presence, and must be supported by the certificate of incorporation, the SPAC trust agreement, and identification of directors and officers.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: The CBCA/QBCA business corporation is a separate juridical person and a 'taxable Canadian corporation' resident in Canada, taxed under ITA Part I on worldwide income at a combined statutory headline rate of approximately 26.5% (federal general rate 15% plus Quebec general rate 11.5%). A listed SPAC is a 'public corporation' under ITA s. 89(1) and cannot elect CCPC status or claim the small business deduction; trust-escrow investment income is taxed at the corporate level, and non-resident shareholders are subject to Part XIII withholding (25% statutory, treaty-reduced, e.g., 15% for portfolio dividends under the Canada-US treaty). Territorial Scope: no territorial exclusion applies to a resident corporation; foreign-source income is fully reportable on the T2 return.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no check-the-box classification: corporate tax identity is statutory, not elective. Relevant mechanisms for a SPAC include: (i) voluntary GST/HST/QST registration under ETA s. 240(1) even below the CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold; (ii) the ETA s. 156 election to treat closely related Canadian corporations as a single GST/HST registrant; (iii) elections for annual or fiscal-year GST/HST reporting periods where the registrant qualifies; (iv) hybrid mismatch and earnings-stripping rules under ITA ss. 18.2-18.6, which afford no protective exclusion for SPAC financing structures; and (v) section 216/217 elections available only to qualifying non-resident investors, not to the resident SPAC itself.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal value-added tax at 5%) plus Quebec Sales Tax (QST at 9.975%); Quebec is not an HST-participating province, and Revenu Québec administers QST separately, producing a combined headline consumer tax rate of 14.975% (5% GST + 9.975% QST).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 — the identical GST/HST and QST small-supplier threshold: registration is compulsory once worldwide taxable supplies (excluding exempt financial services) exceed CAD 30,000 in the current calendar quarter or in any four consecutive calendar quarters. A SPAC's escrow interest income is not consideration for a taxable supply, but sponsor arrangement and trustee oversight fees may be taxable and can trigger the registration obligation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada imposes no real-time fiscal clearance, transaction-level API pre-clearance, or digital stamping regime (contrast the CFDI/NF-e models). Mandates include: (1) registrants must issue a prescribed tax invoice under ETA s. 221(1) and QSTA s. 235 showing the supplier's BN/NEQ, date, recipient identification for supplies above CAD 150, description, and tax amounts; (2) electronic filing of GST/HST and QST returns is compulsory for corporate registrants and for those with annual taxable supplies exceeding CAD 1 million, using CRA NETFILE/XML and Revenu Québec's electronic services; (3) both authorities rely on post-filing risk assessment and data matching rather than pre-clearance; (4) the federal Pan-Canadian E-Invoicing framework (Peppol BIS 3.0) is available for B2B/B2G e-invoicing through certified service-provider APIs but remains voluntary as of 2025.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exports are zero-rated under ETA Schedule VI Part V and the corresponding QSTA provisions where the supplier exports goods from Canada and retains prescribed proof-of-export documentation within two years. For a SPAC, the operative rule is ETA Schedule VI Part IX s. 7: a supply of a financial service to a non-resident recipient (e.g., underwriting, sponsor-acquisition advisory, or trust-escrow management services billed to a non-resident target or investor) is zero-rated where the financial service is not for consumption in Canada; the SPAC must obtain contemporaneous evidence of the recipient's non-resident status (Form RC67-V, tax-residence certificate, or incorporation records), and CRA practice applies a 180-day benchmark for receipt of the foreign consideration.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Export Declaration (Form B13A or the CBSA CERS electronic export report) and carrier-issued Bill of Lading / waybill proving physical export
Commercial invoice identifying the non-resident buyer and the HS classification of any exported goods
Inward Remittance Certificate, SWIFT wire records, or bank statements proving receipt of the foreign currency consideration

Non-resident status and purpose evidence: Form RC67-V (GST/HST certificate for non-resident recipients) or equivalent, plus the SPAC's trust agreement, underwriting agreement, and board minutes documenting the offshore supply
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are a priority audit area. CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess within four years (unlimited where misrepresentation is shown), retroactively claw back zero-rating and input tax credits, and charge interest under ETA s. 280. Civil penalties include the ETA s. 285 failure/incorrect-filing penalty, the ETA s. 327.1 false-statement penalty of 25% of the net tax sought to be evaded, and the ITA s. 163(2) gross-negligence penalty of 50% of the tax avoided. Criminal exposure arises under ETA s. 327 and Criminal Code s. 380 (fraud), with fines and imprisonment; Revenu Québec applies parallel penalties under the Quebec Tax Administration Act and may suspend or revoke the QST registration. Directors and the SPAC sponsor are jointly and severally liable for unremitted GST/HST/QST under ETA s. 323 and the equivalent Quebec regime.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) - Canada maintains no dedicated foreign-exchange administration agency; monetary policy, payment-system oversight, and banking supervision are distributed among the Bank of Canada, the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for Schedule I chartered banks, the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) for cross-border electronic-fund-transfer and AML/ATF reporting, and the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) of Quebec as principal securities regulator for the SPAC reporting issuer.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible on both current and capital accounts; no exchange-control law, capital-inflow licensing, or profit-remittance approval exists. Dividends, redemption proceeds, and escrowed SPAC trust funds may be remitted cross-border freely, subject only to Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) CRS/FATCA reporting and Part XIII non-resident withholding tax (statutory 25 percent base rate, treaty-reducible). The floating CAD regime implies that the SPAC treasury must budget for spot-rate volatility on USD/CAD trust rebalancing.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable - Canada imposes no statutory surrender, mandatory conversion ratio, or repatriation timeline on export proceeds or other foreign receipts. A Quebec-domiciled SPAC may retain, convert, and disburse export or investment proceeds in any currency without Bank of Canada authorization.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a primary banking rail; permissible only as an ancillary FX and collection utility. Canada does not recognize offshore electronic-money-institution (EMI) licenses; platforms such as Wise, Revolut Business, or Airwallex may provide multi-currency wallets and spot conversion, but they are not Schedule I chartered banks and cannot act as escrow agent or custodian for a reporting-issuer SPAC trust, nor satisfy AMF/TSX escrow conditions. Any fintech usage must be confined to non-trust operational disbursements with segregated client funds.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Hybrid mandate with enhanced due diligence escalation: the PCMLTFA permits remote account opening, yet the Medium_Risk_Enhanced SPAC classification (blank-check vehicle, non-resident sponsors, pooled investor funds) prompts Tier 1 Canadian banks to require at least one executive director (CEO or CFO) to complete an in-branch or live video-verified interview with a designated corporate-banking officer; signature verification must be witnessed by a Canadian branch officer or certified by a Canadian notary or commissioner of oaths; non-resident directors must provide certified passport copies, bank reference letters, and source-of-wealth declarations. A physical closing meeting in Montreal or Toronto materially accelerates onboarding to four to eight weeks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial-ownership chain via SPAC sponsor entity, nominee shareholders, or intermediate Delaware/Cayman holding vehicles.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec transparency-register extract; statutory register of directors and beneficial owners; share and unit capital ledger; notarized declarations of ultimate natural persons holding 10 percent or more; sponsor trust deed and operating agreement; organizational chart; escrow and unit-holder agreement waterfall; signed KYC attestation from each sponsor principal.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unverifiable source of funds for IPO and PIPE proceeds injected into the escrow trust.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: AMF final prospectus receipt; SEDAR+ filing confirmation; subscription and placement-agent agreements; CIRO-member investment-dealer AML certification; investor KYC and qualified-investor certificates; funded capital bank statements; independent auditor escrow confirmation; audited opening balance sheet.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident promoter and director nexus with potential politically exposed person (PEP) exposure in the sponsor group.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP declarations for all directors, officers, and 10 percent shareholders; sponsor and management due-diligence memorandum; conflict-of-interest and insider-reporting filings; professional references for each non-resident director; CRA tax-clearance confirmations; evidence of compliance with Quebec Business Corporations Act director residency requirements if applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Regulatory authorisation and statutory-licence uncertainty; bank unable to verify the entity's SPAC and reporting-issuer permission.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: AMF and Canadian Securities Administrators reporting-issuer certificates; TSX conditional listing approval; approved escrow agreement and trust indenture; CIRO membership certificates for sponsoring dealers; continuous disclosure filings including annual information form, management discussion and analysis, and audited financial statements; auditor consent letters; AMF no-default confirmation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Sponsor, PIPE, and institutional funds route via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 for cross-border wires, or via the Payments Canada high-value system (LVTS transitioning to Lynx) for domestic CAD; the remittance-information field 70 must cite the subscription agreement and deal reference to enable matching. Funds credit directly to the ring-fenced SPAC trust account at the Canadian chartered bank; USD/CAD conversions are executed at negotiated spot rates with the call-account bank. FINTRAC electronic-fund-transfer reporting applies for wires equal to or exceeding CAD 10,000; the escrow agent must match each credit against subscriber identity, offering record, documentary conditions precedent, and sanctions and source-of-wealth screening before trust acceptance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational expenses clear through the Payments Canada high-value system for domestic CAD or SWIFT MT103 for cross-border payments funded from the operational account. Escrow releases for the qualifying acquisition, shareholder redemptions, and deferred-underwriting fees are executed only by the escrow agent pursuant to the escrow agreement and AMF/TSX release conditions, using SWIFT MT103 or MT202 or the domestic high-value rail. Cross-border trade settlements for target acquisitions may be supported by commercial letters of credit governed by UCP600 and issued by the relationship bank with correspondent-bank confirmation in the target jurisdiction. All outbound FX conversions must be executed at spot with the primary bank and documented in treasury records supporting the auditor's trust report.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable CAD/USD forwards under ISDA 1998 FX Definitions
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) limited to exotic-currency exposures in target-acquisition jurisdictions
FX swaps for trust-proceeds currency repositioning between CAD and USD
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCIRS) for long-dated acquisition or refinancing liabilities
European-style FX options (premium-paid) executed with a CIRO-regulated dealer under an ISDA and CSA collateral annex; speculative trading expressly prohibited by the SPAC treasury policy

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Update Declaration (declaration de mise a jour annuelle) of the enterprise under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (LPLE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days of each anniversary of the REQ registration date, or within 60 days of the fiscal year end recorded in the register; separate amending declaration required within 60 days of any material change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No automatic late fee on initial default; after formal REQ notice and expiry of a minimum 60-day corrective period, the Registrar may strike the enterprise off the register and administratively dissolve the corporation; general offence penalties may also apply under LPLE sections 30 and 31

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return under section 263 of the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA) (applicable if the SPAC is federally incorporated or is a CBCA extra-provincial registrant in Quebec)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days following each anniversary of the date of incorporation or amalgamation; filed annually in every calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors and officers may be prosecuted for a summary conviction offence under CBCA section 263 with fines of up to CAD 5,000; continued non-filing for at least two consecutive years permits Corporations Canada to dissolve the corporation administratively under CBCA section 212

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Reporting issuer annual continuous disclosure package: audited annual financial statements, Management's Discussion & Analysis, and Annual Information Form under National Instrument 51-102 (triggered when the SPAC completes an IPO, qualifying acquisition, or otherwise becomes a reporting issuer in Quebec)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Autorite des marches financiers (AMF) via the SEDAR+ portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the issuer's financial year end; exchange listing rules (TSX/NEO) or prospectus undertakings may impose earlier filing deadlines
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Placement on regulatory default lists, late-filing fee exposures under NI 51-102, issuance of a failure-to-file cease trade order, possible administrative monetary penalties, and risk of revocation of reporting issuer status for chronic non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholders' meeting and maintenance of corporate minute book (agenda, notices, quorum proof, resolutions, and approved minutes) (corporate record, not a government filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate records office located in Quebec, subject to shareholder inspection and, if applicable, inspection by the AMF as securities regulator
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual meeting must be held no later than 15 months after the previous meeting and within 18 months after incorporation under CBCA/QBCA equivalent requirements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Any shareholder may petition the Superior Court of Quebec for an order directing the holding of the meeting; persistent non-compliance may support an oppression remedy claim and liability for directors' breach of fiduciary duties

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: For a SPAC (ISIC 6499) structured as a Canadian corporation, no revenue or asset threshold removes the audit obligation: an independent audit is compulsory because investor capital is held in trust/escrow and a public listing is the commercial purpose. Once the entity becomes a reporting issuer, NI 51-102 mandates annually audited financial statements in all cases. A private CBCA/QBCA company could technically waive audit by unanimous shareholder consent (CBCA section 150(2) and QBCA equivalent), but such waiver is commercially inapplicable for a SPAC safeguarding shareholder funds and preparing for a prospectus transaction.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB, mandated for reporting issuers under National Instrument 52-107; IFRS is also the required framework for the SPAC's Quebec statutory accounting and trust fund reporting. ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) is unavailable once the entity undertakes or files for a public listing.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec LPLE requires every registered legal person to maintain a register of beneficial owners identifying any individual holding at least 25% of voting shares or de facto control, and to confirm/update that information annually as part of the REQ annual update declaration; material ownership or share transfer changes must be reflected promptly. Under the CBCA, a register of individuals with significant control must be updated within 15 days of any relevant transfer or change, and the information is subject to disclosure in the federal annual return. For the SPAC, trust arrangements and escrow holdings do not obscure UBO status, and nominee or bearer holdings are prohibited.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Beneficial Owners (individuals with significant control under Quebec LPLE and CBCA)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 200 - 450 per year (typical Quebec registered office and registered agent fee for a private Canadian SPAC holding company; higher if the agent concurrently serves as escrow or trust administrator)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 15,000 - 45,000 per year (statutory audit and IFRS financial statements; fee increases for a public or reporting-issuer SPAC requiring trust escrow attestation and SEC/CSA-equivalent comfort procedures)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal 15% plus Quebec 11.5% for a combined general statutory rate of 26.5% (subject to provincial abatement and allocation adjustments; effective combined rate varies by province and active business income level)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small business deduction for Canadian-controlled private corporations (CCPC) on active business income up to CAD 500,000 federally and CAD 500,000 provincially in Quebec, reducing the combined active business rate to approximately 11.0% in Quebec; no statutory general tax holiday for SPACs as the entity is typically a public investment vehicle; investment income is generally not eligible for the small business deduction and is subject to refundable dividend tax rules (RDTOH).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return filed via the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) 'My Business Account' or E-file/T2 electronic filing service. Quebec: CO-17 Corporation Income Tax Return and CO-17.S-V (Sociétés par actions) filed via Revenu Québec's 'Tax Online' portal or authorized E-file software.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Federal T2: no later than two months after the tax year-end for most corporations, or three months for eligible Canadian-controlled private corporations (CCPCs) with a qualifying tax year-end; a six-month extension of filing deadline is available to CCPCs only. Quebec CO-17: due on the last day of the third month following the taxation year-end for CCPCs, otherwise on the last day of the second month following the taxation year-end. Payment of balance due is generally due the same day as the filing deadline without extension.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Box 1 / Line 1 (Federal) and CO-17 Box 1
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification: legal name, business number, registered office address, and corporate status (active, amalgamated, or wound up).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident SPAC must indicate its Canadian branch or permanent establishment address, or if no permanent establishment exists, state 'No permanent establishment in Canada' and complete the waiver and treaty disclosure schedules if relying on the Canada-Quebec tax treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxation year-end and type (ordinary, short fiscal period, or deemed year-end on incorporation, acquisition of control, or winding-up).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities must align the Canadian return with the deemed Canadian fiscal period triggered by Canadian activity; if none, use the statutory Canadian year-end of December 31 unless an approved alternative is obtained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Box 6 / Line 3 (Federal) and CO-17 Box 6
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate status and residency status: resident, non-resident, or deemed resident under the Income Tax Act (Canada) and Quebec Taxation Act.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Select 'Non-resident' and attach the applicable treaty non-residency certificate; for a SPAC structured as a foreign blank-check corporation, confirm no place of central management and control in Canada.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal business activity and North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code; for a SPAC, typically NAICS 525990 (Other Financial Investment Activities).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Describe the SPAC's investment mandate (acquisition of an unidentified operating business) and list the Canadian trust or escrow account arrangement if a Canadian permanent establishment is claimed to exist.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income (loss) before taxes, including interest income from trust/escrow accounts, dividends, and gains or losses from investments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report Canadian-source investment income only; foreign-source income must be segregated and treaty protected unless attributable to a Canadian permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital cost allowance (CCA) and amortization; SPACs generally hold no depreciable assets other than office equipment and leasehold improvements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If no Canadian permanent establishment, claim no CCA; any CCA claimed on Canadian assets reinforces the existence of a permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable dividends received or paid; for a SPAC, dividends or distributions to foreign founders or public shareholders before the de-SPAC transaction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders face Part XIII withholding tax on Canadian-source dividends unless reduced by treaty; indicate the relevant treaty article and the residency of each recipient.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provincial corporate allocation: Quebec taxable income allocation and the Quebec capital tax levy, where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident SPAC with no permanent establishment in Quebec allocates zero income to Quebec; if the SPAC is incorporated under the Canada Business Corporations Act but managed from outside Canada, no Quebec allocation is required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credit calculation for taxes paid to foreign jurisdictions (including U.S. or Cayman taxes) on the same income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim foreign tax credits only if the SPAC is resident in Canada; a Canadian-resident SPAC may credit foreign withholding taxes against Canadian federal and Quebec tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable capital and capital gains, including deemed dispositions and changes in fair market value of SPAC shares held in escrow.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents are generally exempt from Canadian capital gains on shares of a Canadian corporation unless the shares are 'taxable Canadian property' (e.g., a SPAC whose shares are principally listed on a Canadian stock exchange); include the treaty tie-breaker analysis.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Federal: late filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month for up to 12 months for first-time offenders; repeat failure penalty increased to 10% plus 2% per month. Quebec: similar penalty under s. 1079.1 of the Quebec Taxation Act. Failure to file electronically, failure to provide complete schedules, or failure to report Canadian-source income may incur additional penalties of CAD 100 to CAD 2,500 per return, daily surcharges of up to CAD 100 for repeated refusals, and interest (CRA prescribed rates, currently based on three-month Treasury bill plus 2% for tax debts).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Part XIII withholding tax: 25% on dividends paid by a Canadian-resident corporation to a non-resident shareholder, subject to reduction under the Canada-Quebec income tax treaty to 15% generally, 5% for corporate shareholders holding at least 10% voting control, and 0% for certain treaty exemptions; a 25% Quebec withholding tax also applies on distributions to non-residents outside treaty protection.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief, the non-resident shareholder must provide the Canadian payer with a properly completed NR301 (Non-Resident Claim for Tax Treaty Reduction) for Canada and RL-15 or related form for Quebec, or an equivalent NR301-S, before the dividend payment date. The payor must retain the certificate of residency (TRC) issued by the non-resident's home tax authority evidencing residency in the treaty jurisdiction. The TRC must be issued by the relevant competent authority and translated/notarized if necessary. If a TRC is not supplied in time, the full 25% withholding applies; refund claims may be made on the NR7/NR7-S (Refund of Part XIII Tax Withheld) within the limitation period (generally four years from the end of the calendar year). For a SPAC listed on a Canadian exchange, the clearing house and transfer agent must obtain and validate treaty forms for each foreign shareholder.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: statutory 25%; treaty reduced to 0% under Canada-Quebec DTA interest article for arm's-length recipients, and generally 10% for non-arm's length or participating debt interests. Royalties for IP: statutory 25%; treaty reduced to 10% for copyright, patent, trademark, and know-how royalties, and 0% for certain software copyright royalties. Quebec withholding mirrors treaty rates at the provincial level.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 in annual gross revenue from transactions with non-resident related parties (Quebec and federal) triggers mandatory Local File preparation; Master File required when total group revenue exceeds CAD 50 million. Aggregate related-party cross-border transactions exceeding CAD 5 million require full contemporaneous documentation under CRA Information Circular IC 87-2R and Revenu Québec's TP guidance.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP (Comparable Uncontrolled Price) for financial services and interest rates
Resale Price Method for distribution of securities
Cost Plus Method for administrative and management fee services
TNMM (Transactional Net Margin Method) for investment holding and management entities
Profit Split Method for integrated financial activities and shared risk SPAC structures
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) under section 245 of the Income Tax Act and Quebec equivalent under section 1079.1 of the Quebec Taxation Act may recharacterize a SPAC arrangement lacking economic substance. Case law (e.g., Canada Trustco, Copthorne, and the 2020 amendments broadening GAAR) applies a two-step test: a tax benefit exists and the transaction is an avoidance transaction that defeats the object, spirit, or purpose of the relevant provisions. For a Quebec SPAC, Economic Substance Regulations similar to those in other provinces are not codified, but Quebec's anti-avoidance provisions and the federal 'piercing the corporate veil' doctrine in tax matters require genuine commercial activity or investment purpose; a SPAC that is a bare holding company without any real Canadian office, employees, or investment activities may be deemed a sham and subject to reassessment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly or deliberately omitting Canadian-source trust interest income, misrepresenting the trust/escrow account as foreign, false attribution of income to a non-resident, or claiming false deductions for SPAC formation and underwriting costs.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of 50% of the understated tax plus interest; criminal prosecution under section 238 of the Income Tax Act and 75.2 of the Quebec Taxation Act subject to a fine of not less than 50% of the evaded tax and up to 200% thereof, and imprisonment of between 2 and 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers are jointly and severally liable for withholding tax deductions and unpaid corporate tax liabilities under section 227.1 ITA and 30.0.6 of the Quebec Taxation Act; civil assessment of up to 100% of the unremitted amounts, travel bans under Quebec tax enforcement procedures, and imprisonment for willful non-remittance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Incorporating a Quebec SPAC with no real economic activity, no office, no employees, no board meetings in Quebec, and using the corporate vehicle solely to channel investment income to non-residents or to avoid Canadian tax on trust earnings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR reassessment denying the tax benefit, recharacterization of the SPAC's income as the shareholder's income, 50% gross-negligence penalty, and potential application of the 'factual entity' doctrine permitting the CRA or Revenu Québec to ignore the separate identity of the shell corporation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts may pierce the corporate veil and hold directors personally liable for the entire corporate tax deficiency if the corporation is found to be a sham or if directors signed false returns; Quebec civil liability under the Civil Code of Quebec (art. 317) permits an order for restitution and punitive damages; criminal exposure up to 5 years imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Anti-Money Laundering and Unlicensed Investment Business
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a SPAC without registering as a securities issuer/market participant in Quebec, failing to hold the required escrow account under Canadian securities laws, failing to comply with FINTRAC client identity verification and transaction reporting, or accepting investor funds without AML controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Provincial securities commission cease-trade orders, administrative monetary penalties of up to CAD 15,000,000 per violation under the Quebec Securities Act, or CAD 5,000,000 per contravention under federal AML law; criminal fines of up to CAD 500,000 and imprisonment of up to 5 years for failure to report suspicious transactions or money laundering.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a SPAC that executes an unlawful merger without regulatory approval may be personally liable for investor losses; the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) may impose lifetime bans on serving as officers or directors and enforce personal monetary sanctions under the Quebec Securities Act.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to File or False Statements
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful failure to file the T2 or CO-17 return, false declaration of no permanent establishment in Canada, or submitting a materially inaccurate NR301 that causes under-withholding at source.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late-filing penalty equal to 5% of the unpaid amount plus 1% per month (maximum 12 months), repeat-filing penalty increased to 10% plus 2% per month; false-statement penalties under section 163(2) of 50% of the understated liability; Quebec penalties under section 1079.1.1 of up to 200% of the amount evaded, and criminal fine of up to CAD 200,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers who sign tax returns with knowledge of false particulars are personally liable for the penalties and may be prosecuted criminally; travel bans issued by Revenu Québec can prevent departure from Canada for delinquency; imprisonment of up to 2 years for evasion and 12 months for failure to comply with a production demand.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends or management fees to a non-resident investor without applying the correct withholding tax, or without obtaining the foreign shareholder's treaty residency certificate, or distributing trust proceeds in the form of a return of capital disguised as a dividend to avoid Part XIII withholding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Canadian resident corporation is liable for the entire unwithheld amount under subsection 215(1) of the Income Tax Act and Quebec equivalent, plus interest and penalties of up to 100% of the unremitted amount; the non-resident shareholder may also be assessed directly and subjected to garnishment of Canadian assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve undisclosed dividend distributions without an appropriate withholding remittance are personally liable for the unpaid withholding tax under section 227.1 ITA; in egregious cases, directors personally owe the full tax, interest, and penalties, and may be prohibited from trading or leaving Canada until payment is secured.
